prompt:
Create one finished Korean neighborhood repair workshop promotional poster for social media/community display, a single flat opaque 16:9 landscape artwork. Use case: ads-marketing. This is one continuous lived-in human scene: a wide shared worktable viewed obliquely from above spans the full width and depth of the image, with two adult neighbors working at its opposite ends. The table edges, the cropped chair, the spread garment and the neighbors' reaching arms create the composition and guide the eye into a generous opening in the center, where the typography belongs. No separate right text column.

The left neighbor bends attentively over a real wooden chair set against the near table end, one hand steadying its loose seat/leg joint. The other hand receives a clearly identifiable screwdriver being offered handle-first by the right neighbor. Show that hand-to-hand exchange as one simple unambiguous contact near the table's far edge, with the tool, its handle and each person's hand readable. The right neighbor has a torn coral garment spread on the same table; their free hand holds its torn edge beside visible repair stitches, needle and spool. Cloth trails inward along the shared table, joining the two repair activities. Their bodies and working postures are credible: two arms per person, clear ownership of each hand, supported objects and coherent chair joinery. Faces can be simplified, quietly engaged, looking toward the work. Frame the people, chair and fabric at substantial scale, cropped naturally at the far left/right and foreground edges. Keep the two actions connected through the same table, no separate vignettes, panel frames or comparison layout. A few real screws, a spool and scissors lie beside their corresponding work, away from the copy. No arbitrary decorative objects.

Painterly gouache with bold, deliberate silhouettes, matte opaque paint, precise cut edges and nuanced color variation within broad brush-painted forms. Warm coral surrounds the scene, the deep aubergine figures and chair shadows create strong framing weight, and a light yellow-green table creates a luminous shared center. Garment folds and chair joints have enough localized detail to express repair, with subtly visible painted grain and fabric texture. Keep the painting rich and controlled without glossy clay, plastic rendering or noisy texture. The setting is defined by working bodies, tangible repair and the table, never an empty studio wall.

Resolve the central readable body area before scaling the headline. Design for comfortable reading at a 720px-wide community feed as a working display assumption. The central opening is broad enough for a substantial three-line explanation in approximately 15–17px apparent body size at that display. The title is expressive but restrained relative to the entire working scene, around twice the body size rather than a gigantic heading. Use mature precisely printed upright Korean sans-serif with square stable widths, low stroke contrast, open internal counters, balanced consonant/vowel proportions, moderate medium weight and clean word spaces. Align Latin, numerals and punctuation optically with the Korean; small copy has no brush texture. Typography is a flat graphic plane over the painting, fully upright and horizontal, never foreshortened or bent onto the physical table.

The English line sits just above the central title opening. The main title follows that opening, then the short statement and the broad contiguous explanatory paragraph immediately below it, with a stable left starting axis and calm line spacing. Wrap the explanation only at meaningful word boundaries, into three balanced lines without changing any words. Beneath that paragraph, along the same table-directed reading route, place the event name with date, time and place as one coherent group, and immediately beside it place fee, deadline, invitation and URL as the next participation group. Both groups remain large and comfortably readable in the center, without enclosing boxes or a narrow footer. The chair's near edge and inward fabric shape link these groups back to the repair actions. Use deep aubergine copy on the yellow-green opening with clear contrast; preserve enough breathing room around every line, no illustration overlaps text. Information should be naturally discoverable in one connected central reading area, not scattered among corners.

Print only the following twelve copy entries, each exactly once. Preserve every Korean/Latin character, numeral, punctuation mark, uppercase/lowercase and meaningful word space. Soft line wrapping is allowed. Do not print the spec, copy-entry labels or any additional wording:
고쳐 쓰는 토요일
